CVE-2026-98393.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net: ipv4: Fix UDP length overflow with PMTU discover and big MTU

This commit bounds cork->base.fragsize to IP_MAX_MTU to avoid a
possible overflow of UDP length that triggers a WARN in
udp_set_len_short when setsockopt IP_MTU_DISCOVER is set to
IP_PMTUDISC_PROBE, and a large packet is sent over a netdev with an
unusually large MTU.

Steps to reproduce:

1. Set device MTU bigger than IP_MAX_MTU + 20. cork->base.fragsize will
   be set to that MTU in ip_setup_cork.
2. Set IP_MTU_DISCOVER to IP_PMTUDISC_PROBE. It lets maxnonfragsize be
   set to device MTU (cork->fragsize) in __ip_append_data, rather than
   to IP_MAX_MTU.
3. Send 65528 bytes of payload (+8 bytes of UDP header, +20 bytes of
   IPv4 header). Device MTU allows it (it's only one byte bigger than
   IP_MAX_MTU + IPv4 header, and the device MTU is bigger than that).
4. The UDP length in the built packet is 65536, which overflows the
   16-bit length field and triggers the WARN in udp_set_len_short.

Note: IP_PMTUDISC_DO with IPv4 is safe, because ip_dst_mtu_maybe_forward
always clamps at IP_MAX_MTU, unlike ip6_dst_mtu_maybe_forward.

The Fixes tag points at the first commit where I could reproduce the
overflow with IPv4 and IP_PMTUDISC_PROBE.

CVE-2026-98395.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

powerpc/entry: Fix irq_soft_mask corruption on replayed interrupt exit

When __replay_soft_interrupts() replays a pending interrupt (e.g.
PACA_IRQ_DEC -> timer_interrupt), it calls the handler directly with a
synthetic pt_regs. The DEFINE_INTERRUPT_HANDLER_ASYNC wrapper around
each handler calls arch_interrupt_async_exit_prepare() on the way out,
which calls arch_interrupt_exit_prepare() -> local_irq_disable() ->
arch_local_irq_disable(), which does:

    irq_soft_mask_set(IRQS_DISABLED)   /* 0x1 */

This unconditionally overwrites irq_soft_mask with IRQS_DISABLED (0x1),
stripping the IRQS_PMI_DISABLED (0x2) bit. The result is that
irq_soft_mask is 0x1 instead of IRQS_ALL_DISABLED (0x3) when the
handler returns to __replay_soft_interrupts().

For a normally-taken interrupt this is harmless: the next interrupt
always enters through arch_interrupt_enter_prepare() which
unconditionally sets irq_soft_mask to IRQS_ALL_DISABLED. But during
replay, next_interrupt() is called directly between replayed handlers
without going back through arch_interrupt_enter_prepare(), so the
stripped bit is never restored. next_interrupt() then fires a WARNING:

    WARNING: arch/powerpc/kernel/irq_64.c:75
    WARN_ON(irq_soft_mask_return() != IRQS_ALL_DISABLED)

The warning was observed early in boot on a POWER10 pseries guest
during kmem_cache_init_late(), where a spinlock release triggers
interrupt replay that processes a pending timer interrupt.

Debugger state confirming the bug:
  Before timer_interrupt(&regs):
    irq_soft_mask = 0x3 (IRQS_ALL_DISABLED)   correct
    irq_happened  = 0x41 (HARD_DIS|REPLAYING)  correct
  After timer_interrupt(&regs) returns:
    irq_soft_mask = 0x1 (IRQS_DISABLED)        WRONG - PMI bit stripped
    irq_happened  = 0x41                        unchanged

The fix is to replace local_irq_disable() with hard_irq_disable().

hard_irq_disable() is the right primitive here for two reasons:

1. On PPC64 (hw_irq.h:301) it calls irq_soft_mask_set_return(IRQS_ALL_DISABLED),
   setting the soft mask to 0x3 (both IRQS_DISABLED and IRQS_PMI_DISABLED),
   which preserves the PMI bit and fixes the WARNING. The additional
   work it does (__hard_irq_disable(), PACA_IRQ_HARD_DIS |=) is
   redundant but safe since both are already set at this point in the
   exit path; the trace_hardirqs_off() inside is guarded by
   if (!arch_irqs_disabled_flags(flags)) so it will not double-fire.

2. On PPC32 (hw_irq.h:467) hard_irq_disable() maps to
   arch_local_irq_disable() -> __hard_irq_disable(), which clears
   MSR[EE] in hardware. This is exactly correct: PPC32 has no soft-mask
   PACA mechanism, so the hardware disable is the right way to satisfy
   irqentry_exit()'s requirement. This also fixes a build error on PPC32
   where irq_soft_mask_set() is only defined under CONFIG_PPC64:

       arch/powerpc/include/asm/entry-common.h:273: error: implicit
       declaration of function 'irq_soft_mask_set'

   Using hard_irq_disable() requires no #ifdef and is consistent with
   how the rest of the entry code (e.g. entry-common.h:463) handles the
   same PPC32/PPC64 split.

CVE-2026-98396.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

powerpc: Do not restore KUAP in arch_exit_to_user_mode_prepare()

KUAP means kernel cannot touch user memory unless it explicitly is
enabled. In the kernel it should stay AMR_KUAP_BLOCKED. While returning
to userspace just before RFI, kernel should restore the user AMR value
back.

Looks like GENERIC_ENTRY might be treating arch_exit_to_user_mode_prepare()
as the last architecture step before returning to userspace.
commit bee25f97ad24 ("powerpc: Enable GENERIC_ENTRY feature")
therefore called kuap_user_restore() from that hook. But on PowerPC that
is too early. After irqentry_exit() / syscall_exit_to_user_mode() we
still run platform specific exit routines.

e.g. code snippets showing both exception handling and system call
handling as the callers of function arch_exit_to_user_mode_prepare()
which does kuap_user_restore(). The below path shows that calling
kuap_user_restore() is too early when called from
arch_exit_to_user_mode_prepare().

Exception handling in exceptions-64s.S
=======================================

bl	CFUNC(do_page_fault)
	  ..DEFINE_INTERRUPT_HANDLER_ASYNC(do_page_fault)
	      arch_interrupt_async_enter_prepare(regs);
	      state = irqentry_enter(regs);
	      instrumentation_begin();
	      irq_enter_rcu();
	      handler(regs);
	      nap_adjust_return(regs);
	      irq_exit_rcu();
	      instrumentation_end();
	      arch_interrupt_async_exit_prepare(regs);
	      irqentry_exit(regs, state); 		   <<< too early
	        irqentry_exit_to_user_mode()
		  __exit_to_user_mode_prepare(regs, EXIT_TO_USER_MODE_WORK_IRQ);
		    arch_exit_to_user_mode_prepare(regs, ti_work);  <<< too early
b	interrupt_return_srr
		.. bl	CFUNC(interrupt_exit_user_prepare) <<< already calls kuap_user_restore

prep_irq_for_enabled_exit() retry can run kernel code with IRQs on. So
only when that routine is fully finished is when the user KUAP should be
fully restored which interrupt_exit_user_prepare() already takes care of
before returning.

Similarly for system call handling in interrupt_64.S
======================================================

	bl	CFUNC(system_call_exception)

.Lsyscall_exit:
	addi	r4,r1,STACK_INT_FRAME_REGS
	li	r5,0 /* !scv */
	bl	CFUNC(syscall_exit_prepare)
		  .. kuap_assert_locked();
		     syscall_exit_to_user_mode(regs); <<< too early
		       syscall_exit_to_user_mode_prepare(regs);  <<< too early
 		     kuap_user_restore(regs);         <<< already calls

syscall_exit_prepare(), which can enable IRQs, replay a pending
interrupt, and only then rfi. Those functions already restore KUAP
immediately before rfi.

Note that if we restore the user AMR too early like in the current code
as shown from the code snippets above, then we get the following warning
when CONFIG_PPC_KUAP_DEBUG is enabled:
  WARNING: arch/powerpc/include/asm/book3s/64/kup.h:293 at interrupt_exit_user_prepare+0x1a0/0x1c0
  Hardware name: IBM pSeries (emulated by qemu) POWER10 (architected)
  TRAP: 0700
  LR: c00000000000d8d4 CTR: c0000000021fe500
  MSR: <SF,EE,ME,IR,DR,RI,LE>  CR: 44000804  XER: 20040000
  interrupt_exit_user_prepare+0x1a0/0x1c0
  interrupt_return_srr_user+0x8/0x12c

CVE-2026-98397.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

platform/x86: x86-android-tablets: hold device reference for secondary fwnode teardown

In gpio_secondary_fwnode_init(), acpi_bus_find_device_by_name() returns a
device reference, but the local dev variable is declared with
__free(put_device), dropping the reference at the end of each iteration.
Meanwhile, devm_add_action_or_reset() saves the dev pointer for
gpio_secondary_unset() without incrementing its reference count, which
could lead to a use-after-free during driver teardown if the device is
released in the interim.

Acquire an explicit device reference with get_device() when registering
the devres action, and drop it with put_device() inside
gpio_secondary_unset().

CVE-2026-98398.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

locking/lockdep: Invalidate stale class_cache entries for zapped classes

syzbot reported a lockdep splat hitting DEBUG_LOCKS_WARN_ON(1) in
hlock_class() due to an invalid class_idx:

  WARNING: kernel/locking/lockdep.c:238 at __lock_acquire+0x382/0x2cf0 kernel/locking/lockdep.c:5203
  Workqueue: wg-crypt-wg0 wg_packet_tx_worker
  RIP: 0010:hlock_class kernel/locking/lockdep.c:238 [inline]
  RIP: 0010:check_wait_context kernel/locking/lockdep.c:4870 [inline]
  RIP: 0010:__lock_acquire+0x389/0x2cf0 kernel/locking/lockdep.c:5203
  Call Trace:
   <IRQ>
   lock_acquire+0x106/0x350 kernel/locking/lockdep.c:5886
   _raw_spin_lock+0x2e/0x40 kernel/locking/spinlock.c:173
   tcp_tsq_handler+0x29/0x200 net/ipv4/tcp_output.c:1291
   tcp_tsq_workfn+0x384/0x410 net/ipv4/tcp_output.c:1325
   ...

When a lock class is zapped (e.g. during module unload or key
unregistration), zap_class() clears the class's bit in
lock_classes_in_use and removes it from the class hash table.
However, existing lockdep_map instances embedded in data structures
may still retain a pointer to the zapped class in their class_cache[]
array.

When __lock_acquire() subsequently runs on such a lock, it finds
lock->class_cache[subclass] != NULL, skipping register_lock_class()
and assigning hlock->class_idx to the index of the zapped class. When
check_wait_context() or hlock_class() inspects the held_lock, it finds
!test_bit(class_idx, lock_classes_in_use) and warns. Furthermore, if
the zapped slot is subsequently re-allocated to an unrelated lock key,
the stale class_cache entry would erroneously match the unrelated
class (ABA issue).

Add lock_class_cache_is_valid() to validate that the cached class is
within lock_classes bounds, still allocated in lock_classes_in_use
(using uninstrumented arch_test_bit() in __always_inline context so it
is safe in noinstr contexts like match_held_lock()), and that
class->key matches the expected subkey (taking lockdep_set_subclass()
overrides into account). Also use READ_ONCE()/WRITE_ONCE() when
accessing class_cache[].  If the entry is invalid or stale, fall back
to register_lock_class() / look_up_lock_class().

CVE-2026-98399.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

s390/ipl: Fix NULL deref in dump_reipl without re-IPL parm block

Unlike kdump, which passes the re-IPL parameter block through os_info,
the stand-alone dump passes it through the IPL parm block address and
checksum in lowcore.

Some IPL types, like HMC FTP boot or QEMU direct kernel boot, might not
provide an IPL parameter block. In this case reipl_type_init() selects
IPL_TYPE_UNKNOWN and reipl_block_actual remains NULL. Nevertheless,
dump_reipl_run() unconditionally dereferences it when preparing the
lowcore fields. This may happen to work by chance when address zero
contains readable lowcore data. A zero IPL parameter block address is
then stored in lowcore, causing the stand-alone dumper to enter disabled
wait after completing the dump.

Explicitly store a zero IPL parameter block address and checksum when no
re-IPL parameter block is available. This does not change the behavior:
the stand-alone dumper completes the dump and halts, while valid re-IPL
parameter blocks continue to be handled as before.

CVE-2026-98400.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

s390/ipl: Fix NULL deref in kdump without re-IPL parm block

Some IPL types, like HMC FTP boot or QEMU direct kernel boot, might
not provide an IPL parameter block. In this case, reipl_type_init()
selects IPL_TYPE_UNKNOWN, and reipl_block_actual remains NULL.

kdump passes the re-IPL parameter block to the dump kernel through
os_info. Before commit 3b9678472bab ("s390/ipl: correct kdump reipl
block checksum calculation"), the os_info entry was added only for
IPL types which initialized reipl_block_actual. That commit moved the
os_info update to machine_crash_shutdown(), making it unconditional. As
a result, set_os_info_reipl_block() dereferences reipl_block_actual for
IPL_TYPE_UNKNOWN. This may happen to work by chance when address zero
contains readable lowcore data and the resulting empty os_info entry is
ignored by the dump kernel.

Skip the os_info update when no re-IPL parameter block is available.
Kdump then collect the dump and reboot without setting re-IPL parameter
block.

CVE-2026-98401.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net: iptunnel: fix stale transport header during tunnel decapsulation

Syzbot reported a crash in qdisc_pkt_len_segs_init() caused by a stale
transport_header offset after tunnel decapsulation.

BUG: unable to handle page fault for address: ffffed102091a42e
Oops: Oops: 0000 [#1] SMP KASAN NOPTI
CPU: 0 UID: 0 PID: 340 Comm: qdisc_uaf_repro Not tainted 7.2.0-rc4-00061-g248951ddc14d #256 PREEMPT(full)
Hardware name: QEMU Standard PC (Q35 + ICH9, 2009), BIOS 1.16.3-debian-1.16.3-2 04/01/2014
RIP: 0010:__asan_load2
<IRQ>
qdisc_pkt_len_segs_init (net/core/dev.c:4145)
__dev_queue_xmit (net/core/dev.c:4787)
br_dev_queue_push_xmit (net/bridge/br_forward.c:53)
br_handle_frame_finish (net/bridge/br_input.c:229)
br_handle_frame (net/bridge/br_input.c:315)
__netif_receive_skb_core.constprop.0 (net/core/dev.c:6099)
__netif_receive_skb_list_core (net/core/dev.c:6287)
netif_receive_skb_list_internal (net/core/dev.c:6445)
napi_complete_done (net/core/dev.c:6813)
gro_cell_poll (net/core/gro_cells.c:74)
__napi_poll (net/core/dev.c:7735)
net_rx_action (net/core/dev.c:7798 net/core/dev.c:7955)
handle_softirqs (kernel/softirq.c:622)
do_softirq (kernel/softirq.c:523  kernel/softirq.c:510 )
__local_bh_enable_ip (kernel/softirq.c:450)
tun_get_user (drivers/net/tun.c:1986 (discriminator 1))
tun_chr_write_iter (drivers/net/tun.c:2032)

The issue is completely latent until qdisc read transport header in
commit 7fb4c1967011 ("net: pull headers in qdisc_pkt_len_segs_init()").
The crash requires four conditions to line up:

1. The incoming packet is encapsulated and carries GSO metadata. The outer
   transport header offset is stored in skb->transport_header while the
   packet is still in the outer tunnel context.
2. The tunnel receiver strips the outer headers. skb->data is advanced to
   the inner frame, but skb->transport_header is left pointing to the
   now-removed outer L4 header, so it becomes a negative offset relative to
   the new data.
3. The inner frame is not delivered to the local IP stack. Instead, it
   is forwarded at L2 by a bridge or HSR, so ip_rcv_core() never runs and
   the transport header is not reset to the inner L4 offset.
4. The forwarding path calls __dev_queue_xmit(), which enters
   qdisc_pkt_len_segs_init(). That function computes the GSO header length
   from skb_transport_offset(skb). Because the offset is negative, the
   unsigned cast overflows and pskb_may_pull(skb, hdr_len +
   sizeof(struct tcphdr)) reads past the end of the skb, triggering a
   KASAN fault or page fault.

The issue specifically requires GSO packets (shinfo->gso_size != 0), which
are processed/aggregated through gro_cells. Fix this by clearing
transport_header to the ~0U sentinel in gro_cell for all tunnnel driver.
GTP does not support GRO/GSO, drop the evil GSO packets in GTP directly.

CVE-2026-98402.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net: icmp: avoid invalid transport header access in icmp_send tracepoint

syzbot reported a WARNING triggered by DEBUG_NET_WARN_ON_ONCE():

 WARNING: at skb_transport_header include/linux/skbuff.h:3087 [inline]
 WARNING: at udp_hdr include/linux/udp.h:23 [inline]
 WARNING: at do_trace_event_raw_event_icmp_send include/trace/events/icmp.h:30 [inline]
 WARNING: at trace_event_raw_event_icmp_send+0x48c/0x6ec include/trace/events/icmp.h:11
 Call trace:
  skb_transport_header include/linux/skbuff.h:3087 [inline]
  udp_hdr include/linux/udp.h:23 [inline]
  do_trace_event_raw_event_icmp_send include/trace/events/icmp.h:30 [inline]
  trace_event_raw_event_icmp_send+0x48c/0x6ec include/trace/events/icmp.h:11
  __traceiter_icmp_send include/trace/events/icmp.h:11 [inline]
  __do_trace_icmp_send include/trace/events/icmp.h:11 [inline]
  trace_icmp_send+0x320/0x49c include/trace/events/icmp.h:11
  __icmp_send+0xcfc/0x11d8 net/ipv4/icmp.c:1013
  ipv4_send_dest_unreach net/ipv4/route.c:1280 [inline]
  ipv4_link_failure+0x57c/0x8dc net/ipv4/route.c:1287
  dst_link_failure include/net/dst.h:438 [inline]
  vti_tunnel_xmit+0xe40/0x17a4 net/ipv4/ip_vti.c:307

TP_fast_assign() unconditionally calls udp_hdr(skb) before checking
whether the packet is UDP. Furthermore, __icmp_send() can be invoked
from paths (e.g., link failures, ARP errors, forwarding, AF_PACKET)
where skb->transport_header was never initialized (~0U).

Under CONFIG_DEBUG_NET=y, calling skb_transport_header(skb) triggers
DEBUG_NET_WARN_ON_ONCE(!skb_transport_header_was_set(skb)).

Fix this by:
1. Only parsing transport info when iph->protocol == IPPROTO_UDP.
2. Using skb_header_pointer() at skb_network_offset(skb) + (iph->ihl << 2)
   to safely fetch the UDP header without assuming transport_header is set.

CVE-2026-98403.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

s390/boot: Avoid IPL parameter append past command line

A command line may occupy all but the terminating byte of
COMMAND_LINE_SIZE. In that case append_ipl_block_parm() passes a zero size
to the IPL parameter conversion helpers and points the destination one
byte past early_command_line. The helpers subtract one from the unsigned
size and write the converted parameter outside the command line buffer.

Convert the IPL parameter in the command line parsing buffer first. A
parameter beginning with '=' can then replace the existing command line
regardless of its length, while other parameters are appended only when
space remains.

CVE-2026-98404.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/virtio: Fix a NULL vs ERR_PTR() bug in virtio_gpu_user_framebuffer_create()

Smatch complains that returning a NULL here will lead to a NULL pointer
dereference in drm_mode_addfb2().  Return an error pointer instead.

CVE-2026-98405.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: fix missing iov bounds check in parse_posix_sids()

In parse_posix_sids(), sidsbuf_end is calculated using the server-supplied
out_len without being validated against the actual length of the received
iov (iov_len).

If a server provides an inflated out_len, sidsbuf_end will point past the
end of the iov. This defeats the bounds guards in posix_info_sid_size(),
allowing out-of-bounds reads into adjacent kernel memory.

Fix this by rejecting responses where the calculated sidsbuf_end would
exceed the received iov boundaries or cause pointer wraparound.

CVE-2026-98406.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

wifi: mac80211: avoid WARN in set_bitrate_mask when sdata not in driver

ieee80211_set_bitrate_mask() checks if the interface is running via
ieee80211_sdata_running(), but it does not check if the interface is
still present in the driver.

When sdata is running but IEEE80211_SDATA_IN_DRIVER is not set, the
call reaches drv_set_bitrate_mask() in driver-ops.h which hits

  wlan1: Failed check-sdata-in-driver check, flags: 0x0
  WARNING: net/mac80211/driver-ops.h:884 at drv_set_bitrate_mask

Syzkaller triggers this via wext SIOCSIWRATE ioctl. The Call Trace shows
wext_ioctl_dispatch() in wext-core.c dispatching the ioctl, calling
ioctl_standard_call() for SIOCSIWRATE, which calls cfg80211_wext_siwrate()
in wext-compat.c. That builds a bitrate mask and calls
rdev_set_bitrate_mask() which ends up in ieee80211_set_bitrate_mask() in
cfg.c. The interface is marked running via SDATA_STATE_RUNNING but
flags is 0, so check_sdata_in_driver() fails.

When the interface is being torn down, or when wext ioctl is issued
during interface bringup before drv_add_interface() sets IN_DRIVER, the
running check passes while IN_DRIVER is clear.

Check IEEE80211_SDATA_IN_DRIVER in ieee80211_set_bitrate_mask() before
calling the driver, returning -ENETDOWN. This avoids the WARN_ONCE in
driver-ops.h and matches other cfg.c operations that bail early when not
in driver.

This change should be safe because wiphy mutex is held in
cfg80211_wext_siwrate() via guard(wiphy), and IN_DRIVER is set/cleared
under RTNL and wiphy paths in drv_add_interface() and
drv_remove_interface() in driver-ops.c, so the check is race-free
against driver add/remove. Returning -ENETDOWN is the same error other
not-running paths use and does not introduce new locking.

[also add second syzbot report]

CVE-2026-98407.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

wifi: rsi: fix heap OOB write on key removal

When a key is removed (data == NULL), rsi_hal_load_key() runs:

	memset(&set_key[FRAME_DESC_SZ], 0, frame_len - FRAME_DESC_SZ);

set_key is a struct rsi_set_key *, so the subscript is scaled by
sizeof(struct rsi_set_key) (160 bytes): &set_key[FRAME_DESC_SZ] is
skb->data + 2560, and the memset writes 144 zero bytes starting
2.4KB past the end of the 160-byte skb data buffer, corrupting
unrelated heap objects. The intended byte offset would have been
(u8 *)set_key + FRAME_DESC_SZ.

The write fires on every DISABLE_KEY callback, so plain disconnects,
roams and interface teardowns trigger it on real networks.

The memset is redundant: the whole buffer is zeroed right after
allocation, so the frame sent to the device is byte-identical
without it. Drop the else branch; normal operation is unaffected.

Discovered by Atuin - Automated Vulnerability Discovery Engine.

CVE-2026-98408.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

watchdog: rzv2h: Avoid division by zero

clk_get_rate() could return 0.  Avoid a division by zero panic.

CVE-2026-98409.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

watchdog: rtd119x: Avoid division by zero

clk_get_rate() could return 0.  Avoid a division by zero panic.

CVE-2026-98410.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

watchdog: da9063: fix suspend/resume handling of HW_RUNNING watchdog

da9063_wdt_suspend() and da9063_wdt_resume() only check watchdog_active(),
when the watchdog is left running by the driver sets
WDOG_HW_RUNNING in da9063_wdt_probe() but userspace never opens the
device, so WDOG_ACTIVE remains cleared, the wdt_disable() will not be
executed in da9063_wdt_suspend. In this case, the suspend callback is
a no-op and the watchdog keeps counting during system suspend,
leading to an unexpected system reset.
Check WDOG_HW_RUNNING and wdd，can fix this issue.

CVE-2026-98411.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

power: sequencing: fix NULL-pointer dereference in pwrseq_device_register()

If dev_set_name() fails in pwrseq_device_register(), we jump to the
err_put_pwrseq label before initializing pwrseq->targets.
pwrseq_release() will try to iterate over targets unconditionally and
subsequently dereference an invalid pointer. Move the call to
dev_set_name() after the list head is initialized.

CVE-2026-98412.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

power: sequencing: fix NULL-pointer dereference in pwrseq_unit_new()

If memory allocation fails in pwrseq_unit_setup_deps(), pwrseq_unit_put()
is called to release the partially initialized unit. However, we've
never initialized unit->list and pwrseq_unit_release() will
unconditionally call list_del() on it. Initialize unit->list right after
allocating the unit struct.

CVE-2026-98413.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

selinux: always fill AVC decision in avc_has_perm_noaudit()

avc_has_perm_noaudit() is documented to return a copy of the access
decision in @avd, but its early return for an empty requested permission
set leaves the buffer untouched.  All callers pass an uninitialized
stack variable and afterwards feed it to avc_audit(), and the inode hook
even stores it in the per-task decision cache.

Fill in a deny-all, audit-all decision, similar to avd_init(), so every
caller receives a defined value at no cost on the hot path.

CVE-2026-98414.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

memcg: avoid charging the root memcg from obj_cgroup_charge_pages()

obj_cgroup_charge_pages() resolves the objcg to its memcg and calls
try_charge_memcg(), which does not short circuit the root memcg.  That
memcg can be the root memcg: obj_cgroup_is_root() reflects the memcg the
objcg was created for and is never updated, while memcg_reparent_objcgs()
does redirect objcg->memcg to the parent on rmdir.  An objcg of a dying
child of root therefore passes every obj_cgroup_is_root() filter but
resolves to the root memcg.

Folios keep the objcg they were charged with, so this is easy to reach
through zswap: allocate anon memory in a cgroup, move the task out, remove
the cgroup, then write to the root cgroup's memory.reclaim.  The reclaimed
folios are charged through the reparented objcg and end up in
refill_stock() with the root memcg:

  WARNING: mm/memcontrol.c:2198 at refill_stock+0x644/0x940
   refill_stock+0x644/0x940
   try_charge_memcg+0x12d6/0x1570
   __obj_cgroup_charge+0x35/0xf0
   obj_cgroup_charge+0x1de/0x210
   obj_cgroup_charge_zswap+0x83/0x270
   zswap_store+0x1620/0x2000
   swap_writeout+0x94c/0x14c0
   shrink_folio_list+0x3388/0x52b0
   [...]
   try_to_free_mem_cgroup_pages+0x30d/0x830
   user_proactive_reclaim+0x504/0x840
   memory_reclaim+0x1f/0x30

Beyond the warning, the charge is asymmetric: obj_cgroup_uncharge_pages()
skips refill_stock() for the root memcg, so the root's page counter grows
and is never uncharged.  It is not user visible, since memory.current is
not exposed on the root, but it is a leak.

Use try_charge(), which returns early for the root memcg, restoring the
symmetry with obj_cgroup_uncharge_pages().

The above sequence was scripted into a standalone reproducer (zswap on,
swap on a virtio disk, 512MB of anon memory faulted in inside a child of
the root cgroup, the task then migrated to the root cgroup, the child
removed, followed by "echo 600M swappiness=max > memory.reclaim" on the
root) and run in a CONFIG_DEBUG_VM=y VM.  It reproduces the splat on the
first zswap store of a reparented folio, with the same call chain as the
report.  With this patch applied the splat is gone while the zswap store
count over the run is unchanged, so the same path is still exercised. 
cgroup selftests test_zswap, test_kmem and test_memcontrol show no new
failures.

CVE-2026-98415.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

soc: samsung: exynos-pmu: fix use-after-free of interrupt generator node

The setup_cpuhp_and_cpuidle() parses the device tree node for the
interrupt generation block via of_parse_phandle() and decrements its
reference count using of_node_put() immediately after fetching the resource
address. However, later the intr_gen_node pointer is passed into
of_syscon_register_regmap().

Fix this by declaring intr_gen_node with __free() and removing
of_node_put().

CVE-2026-98416.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

dmaengine: ti: k3-udma-glue: fix NULL dereference in k3_udma_glue_release_rx_chn()

If devm_kcalloc() for rx_chn->flows fails in a channel request function,
the error path calls k3_udma_glue_release_rx_chn(), which dereferences
the NULL rx_chn->flows pointer in k3_udma_glue_release_rx_flow().

Skip the flow release loop in k3_udma_glue_release_rx_chn() when
rx_chn->flows is not allocated.

Found by Linux Verification Center (linuxtesting.org) with SVACE.

CVE-2026-98417.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net: xfrm: reject unrepresentable espintcp transport headers

ESP-in-TCP can hand xfrm packets whose transport header offset no longer
fits after the stream parser trims the TCP envelope. The plain transport
header reset truncates that offset and triggers the skb warning path.

Use the careful transport-header helper and drop the skb through the
existing XFRM error path when the offset cannot be represented.

CVE-2026-98418.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

sched/core: Avoid false migration warning for proxy donors

Proxy execution can move a blocked donor's scheduling context to the
lock owner's CPU even when the donor is migration-disabled. The donor
does not execute there, and its original execution CPU remains recorded
in wake_cpu.

set_task_cpu() warns unconditionally for migration-disabled tasks, so a
subsequent proxy migration or the wakeup path returning the donor home
triggers a false positive: moving a blocked scheduling context does not
violate the migration-disabled execution context.

For example, creating a mutex owner on CPU1 and a migration-disabled
waiter on CPU0 can trigger the following warning:

  proxy_migrate_repro: donor blocking on CPU0 with migration disabled
  proxy_migrate_repro: donor moved from CPU0 to CPU1
  WARNING: kernel/sched/core.c:3389 at set_task_cpu+0x1d3/0x280
  ...
  Call Trace:
   try_to_wake_up+0x43f/0x780
   __mutex_unlock_slowpath+0x330/0x540
   owner_fn+0x9f/0xc0 [proxy_migrate_repro]
  ...
  proxy_migrate_repro: donor woke on CPU0, task_cpu=0
  proxy_migrate_repro: completed

Exclude blocked proxy donors from the warning. The proxy wakeup path
restores an executable placement before clearing the blocked state.

CVE-2026-98420.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: follow SMB2 session expiration semantics

ksmbd_session_register() destroys valid sessions after ten seconds of
inactivity whenever a client starts another SessionSetup exchange. This
confuses Session.IdleTime with Session.ExpirationTime. Windows can create
additional authenticated sessions on an existing connection, so deleting
the older session invalidates its tree connects and makes mapped drives
fail with STATUS_NETWORK_NAME_DELETED.

The session expiration rules require the server to change a valid session
to expired only after its credential expiration time passes. A valid or
expired session otherwise keeps its connection from being scavenged.
Connections that have not negotiated a dialect, have no sessions, or have
only InProgress sessions are disconnected after an implementation-specific
timeout. Use the Windows-compatible 45 second value and run the expiration
check periodically for both TCP and SMB Direct.

Keep zero as an infinite credential expiration time, and count each
Valid-to-Expired transition. Set expired sessions to InProgress when they
reauthenticate. If authentication fails, remove the session from the
global and per-connection tables immediately, including SMB3 multichannel
connections.

Retain protection against abandoned SessionId-zero exchanges by allowing
only one InProgress authentication per connection. Additional exchanges
fail with STATUS_INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES, and stale InProgress sessions are
reaped after the same 45 second setup timeout. This bounds the original
unauthenticated memory-exhaustion path without evicting established
sessions.

CVE-2026-98421.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

wifi: mac80211: require a peer station for TDLS setup confirm

It's nonsense for the setup confirm to go to station that
doesn't even exist, and it hits a warning when building
the frame:

  WARN_ON_ONCE(!sta || !ap_sta)

Only accept WLAN_TDLS_SETUP_CONFIRM when the station is
already there as a TDLS station. Need to copy the call
to ieee80211_tdls_prep_mgmt_packet() since the existing
WLAN_TDLS_DISCOVERY_REQUEST already falls through to it.

CVE-2026-98422.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

wifi: mac80211: reset the AP_VLAN tailroom counter on ifdown

On ifup, AP_VLAN interfaces get crypto_tx_tailroom_needed_cnt from
the AP interface, but it's never decremented again unless the AP is
also brought down. Thus, bringing the same AP_VLAN up again will
increment the counter again and eventually hit the sanity check:

  WARN_ON_ONCE(sdata->crypto_tx_tailroom_needed_cnt !=
               master->crypto_tx_tailroom_needed_cnt);

Reset it on ifdown to avoid that.

CVE-2026-98423.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

wifi: mac80211_hwsim: don't hand frames to mac80211 while stopping

The code checks ->started for frames coming from wmediumd, but the
radio can be stopped after the check and before frame delivery,
causing mac80211 to hit the WARN_ON(!local->started).

Expand the mutex for this case and synchronise against it when the
radio is stopped to avoid being able to hit the warning with hwsim.

Drop the error print that would've complicated the error path, it
only triggers for allocation failures (already noisy) and malformed
frames anyway.

CVE-2026-98424.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

wifi: cfg80211: undo netns switch if renaming the wiphy fails

Once all the interfaces have been moved, cfg80211_switch_netns()
moves the wiphy itself by setting its network namespace and then
renaming it, which makes sysfs move it. The rename can fail (but
only on allocation failures), leaving things mixed up and hitting
the warning there.

Ignoring it isn't great, undo the move and let the change fail
in this case. If undo fails then WARN, then things would again
be stuck in two different network namespaces.

CVE-2026-98425.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

wifi: mac80211: don't warn when an IBSS has no channel to scan

ieee80211_request_ibss_scan() warns when regulatory leaves no
allowed channel, but that can happen as the regdomain can change
while IBSS is operating, and it can continue to operate briefly
during the 60s grace period until it's shut down.

Just remove the warning in this case.

CVE-2026-98426.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

wifi: mwifiex: fix IRQ leak using wrong index in MSI-X error path

mwifiex_pcie_request_irq() registers each MSI-X vector with a per-index
dev_id (&card->msix_ctx[i]). On a request_irq() failure the cleanup loop
"for (j = 0; j < i; j++)" frees msix_entries[j].vector but passes the
failed index's &card->msix_ctx[i] as the dev_id. free_irq() matches on
(irq, dev_id), so it fails to find the action registered with
&card->msix_ctx[j]: the already-requested IRQ j is not freed (leaked) and
free_irq() warns about freeing a non-existent IRQ. Use &card->msix_ctx[j].

CVE-2026-98427.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net/sched: codel: bound the dropping loop per dequeue call

The CoDel control law schedules the next drop one interval/sqrt(count)
after the previous drop, using the configured interval
(codel_params.interval). For very small intervals the scheduled step
rounds down to zero, so the dropping loop in codel_dequeue() never
advances and drains the entire backlog under the qdisc lock in one
call - an unprivileged user can trigger a soft lockup this way.

Fix in the shared codel code used by both codel and fq_codel:

1. Make the control-law step at least 1 tick so the dropping loop
   always moves forward.

2. Cap the dropping loop at CODEL_MAX_DROPS_PER_DEQUEUE (256) drops
   per codel_dequeue() call, resyncing drop_next to now when the cap
   is hit: the catch-up owed to the loop grows with the idle gap and
   the backlog, which no interval threshold can bound. This is a
   deliberate behaviour change after long idle gaps.

The cap applies to fq_codel (4b549a2ef4be) and the mac80211 TXQ path
(fixed interval, cap only).

The target sojourn delay (codel_params.target) is not validated: it
does not feed the control law, so a sub-tick value is aggressive
rather than deadlock-prone.

Conditions to recreate the bug:
  - tc qdisc add dev lo root handle 1: tbf rate 1kbit burst 2kb limit 1000000
  - tc qdisc add dev lo parent 1:1 handle 10: codel interval 2us target 1ms noecn limit 1000000 (same for fq_codel)
  - unpatched kernel: tc accepts it; a UDP flood under the 1kbit tbf
    soft-lockups (watchdog: BUG: soft lockup) while one
    codel_dequeue() call drops the backlog under the qdisc lock
  - patched kernel: same setup, at most 256 drops per dequeue call,
    no soft lockup

Testing: claim reproducer and interval 2us/3us variants run clean;
tdc qdisc category passes (see the selftests patch).

CVE-2026-98428.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ALSA: usb: 6fire: Avoid embedded URBs

The USB 6fire driver uses URBs embedded in different structs for PCM,
MIDI and communication, and this is basically a buggy implementation
nowadays; since a URB is managed with a refcount, this may lead to a
UAF when the URB is released asynchronously.

For addressing the problem, this patch converts those embedded URBs to
ones that are properly allocated via usb_alloc_urb().  The
pcm_urb.packets[] is gone, as it's allocated by usb_alloc_urb(), hence
it's found in urb.iso_frame_desc[] instead.

The conversions are rather straightforward; each embedded struct urb
is changed to a pointer, and its callers are updated accordingly.
The resource for those structs are released in the common destructor
functions (usb6fire_comm_free(), etc), which are called at both the
init error path and the disconnect.

No functional changes, only compile-tested.

CVE-2026-98429.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

RDMA/efa: Keep EQ resources alive while IRQ is registered

The completion IRQ handler accesses the EQ state and DMA buffer. Its IRQ was
registered before that state was initialized, while teardown released the
buffer before free_irq() synchronized the handler.

Initialize the EQ without arming it, register the IRQ, and then arm it.
Reverse the resource order during teardown by freeing the IRQ before
destroying the EQ.

CVE-2026-98430.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

RDMA/efa: Keep admin queues alive while IRQ is registered

The management IRQ handler accesses both the admin completion queue and the
async event queue. The driver registered the IRQ before constructing these
queues and destroyed them before freeing the IRQ, so the handler's lifetime
was not contained by the resources it accesses.

Initialize the queues with interrupts masked, request the IRQ, and then
switch to interrupt mode. On removal, reset the device and free the IRQ
before destroying the queues. Also reset the device before destroying the
queues if IRQ registration fails, because the device already has their DMA
addresses.

CVE-2026-98431.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

RDMA/uverbs: Fix mmap_lock/disassociation_lock circular dependency

Commit 51976c6cd786 ("RDMA/core: Provide rdma_user_mmap_disassociate()
to disassociate mmap pages") introduced disassociation_lock to protect
new mmap registrations against uverbs_user_mmap_disassociate(), but
created an ABBA deadlock:

  Thread A (mmap / fork):
    mmap_lock -> disassociation_lock

  Thread B (disassociate):
    disassociation_lock -> mmap_lock

Fix by removing disassociation_lock entirely and using the pre-existing
hw_destroy_rwsem instead. hw_destroy_rwsem already provides the same
protection: rdma_umap_open() and ib_uverbs_mmap() both use
down_read_trylock() before registering a new VMA, so holding hw_destroy_rwsem
in uverbs_user_mmap_disassociate() is sufficient to block new registrations.
trylock is used in both mmap paths (not blocking down_read) because
mmap_lock is already held on entry, and uverbs_user_mmap_disassociate()
acquires mmap_lock internally — a blocking read would recreate the same
deadlock.

The only caller that was not taking hw_destroy_rwsem for write was
rdma_user_mmap_disassociate(). Fix it to take the rwsem per-ufile while
iterating under lists_mutex.  This is safe because ib_uverbs_close()
releases hw_destroy_rwsem entirely before acquiring lists_mutex, so the
two locks are never held simultaneously.

CVE-2016-20099.description: L-SMASH through 2.14.5 contains an infinite loop vulnerability in vc1_importer_probe() in importer/vc1_imp.c that allows attackers to hang applications via crafted input files. Attackers can supply a file consisting only of zero bytes, which lsmash_read_file() probes automatically, causing indefinite CPU consumption and denial of service.

CVE-2017-20286.description: DevIL through 1.8.0 contains a heap-based buffer overflow in iGetPalette() in il_gif.cpp that allows attackers to write beyond a 768-byte palette buffer when loading GIF images. Attackers can supply a crafted two-frame GIF whose second frame uses disposal method 1 with a local colour table, writing up to 384 controlled bytes past the heap allocation and possibly executing code.

CVE-2020-37281.description: Gravitee API Management through 4.12.22 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to impersonate any user by forging JWTs signed with the shipped default jwt.secret. Attackers knowing an existing user ID can sign an HS256 token with that subject and present it as a bearer token to the Management API, impersonating administrators to gain full platform control.

CVE-2020-37282.description: office-converter through 1.0.2 contains an OS command injection vulnerability that allows attackers to execute commands by supplying a crafted fileName to generatePdf() or generateHtml(). Attackers can embed $(...), backticks, or a closing quote with shell metacharacters in the file name, which is concatenated into an unoconv command run via child_process.exec(), executing commands with Node.js process privileges.

CVE-2024-58392.description: PhysicsFS through 3.2.0 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in __PHYSFS_utf8codepoint() that allows attackers to read past name buffers via an off-by-one cursor advance on six-octet UTF-8 sequences. Attackers can supply a crafted archive with entry names ending in six-octet sequences, causing PHYSFS_utf8stricmp() and hashing to over-read and crash the application.

CVE-2025-71433.description: Kaneo before 2.1.6 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated users to access other workspaces by supplying project, task, label or workspace identifiers to API routes lacking membership checks. Attackers who obtain identifiers, for example from shared project links, can read projects and tasks, modify or delete tasks, labels and comments, and search workspace contents.

CVE-2026-101019.description:
Description
NGINX JavaScript (njs) has a vulnerability where the njs XML module exposes entity-backed XML attributes inconsistently with libxml2 canonicalization. In both the built-in njs and QuickJS backends during the canonicalization process, the $attr$Name getter may return undefined for an explicitly present attribute containing an internal entity reference. The $attrs getter may return a value derived only from the first attribute child. This may allow an unauthenticated attacker that invests significant effort in obtaining a genuinely signed document to skip validation while signature verification succeeds. An nginx-saml deployment is a confirmed affected consumer when run with the built-in njs backend.

Impact
In affected signed-XML consumers, an unauthenticated attacker can cause security-relevant attributes to appear absent or truncated while signature verification succeeds. In nginx-saml, this can bypass expiry, Destination, and request-correlation checks, enabling replay or acceptance of a response outside its intended context. It does not permit signature or identity forgery, or a direct availability impact. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



 Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

CVE-2026-101025.description:
Description


NGINX JavaScript (njs) has a vulnerability where the built-in njs engine leaks a libxml2 parser context when xml.parse() fails. The failure path did not register cleanup and the context was not released for the lifetime of the process. An unauthenticated attacker may send requests with malformed XML and can cause unbounded memory growth in long-lived NGINX worker processes.

Impact


This vulnerability may allow remote attackers to send requests that trigger repeated parsing of malformed XML and may lead to NGINX worker termination or denial of service. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



 Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

CVE-2026-101895.description: Angular is a development platform for building mobile and desktop web applications using TypeScript/JavaScript and other languages. Prior to 20.3.31, 21.2.23, and 22.1.6, the @angular/platform-server DOM emulation parser can enter an infinite synchronous loop when Angular server-side rendering processes attacker-controlled HTML containing an incomplete DOCTYPE that ends with whitespace at end of input. In Domino lib/HTMLParser.js, after_doctype_name_state emits doctype and EOF tokens without advancing nextchar or leaving the fixed-lookahead state, so the scanner repeatedly handles the same EOF marker. A remote unauthenticated attacker can use this condition through server-side HTML parsing paths such as innerHTML binding to consume a Node.js SSR worker at full CPU, starve the event loop, and stop concurrent and subsequent requests. This issue is fixed in versions 20.3.31, 21.2.23, and 22.1.6.

CVE-2026-104939.description:
Description
NGINX Ingress Controller has a vulnerability when implementing an externalAuth policy for ingress. NGINX Ingress Controller may mishandle the HTTP response from an OAuth IdP and allow an attacker to acquire unauthenticated access to protected paths before the proper external authentication can happen.



Impact
This vulnerability may allow remote attackers 

unauthenticated

 access to protected 

paths. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.




Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

CVE-2026-107381.description: svg-sanitizer is a PHP SVG/XML sanitizer. Prior to 1.0.0, Resolver::processReferences() in src/ElementReference/Resolver.php builds the SVG <use> reference graph with a case-sensitive href attribute predicate before cleanHrefAttributes() normalizes mixed-case names. An attacker can provide xlink:HrEf on nested <use> elements so the graph omits those references, after which the sanitizer converts the attribute to canonical xlink:href and returns the live nesting structure without applying the useNestingLimit protection. A consuming application that renders the sanitized SVG can therefore be exposed to the resource exhaustion that control is designed to prevent. This issue is fixed in version 1.0.0.

CVE-2026-110257.description: OW2 ASM 5.0 before 9.11 contains an excessive memory allocation vulnerability in ClassReader.readBootstrapMethodsAttribute() that sizes an int array from num_bootstrap_methods without validating attribute_length. Attackers can supply a crafted class file of about 100 bytes that forces roughly 2 GB allocation, causing an OutOfMemoryError that crashes the JVM or consuming thread.

CVE-2026-110258.description: OW2 ASM 3.0 before 9.11 contains an excessive memory allocation vulnerability in Label.addSubroutineRetSuccessors() that fails to enforce the single-RET-per-JSR rule. Attackers can supply a crafted invalid class file with multiple RET instructions for one JSR, triggering a roughly 2 GB allocation that crashes the JVM.

CVE-2026-110259.description: OW2 ASM 3.0 before 9.11 contains an uncontrolled recursion vulnerability in ClassWriter.replaceAsmInstructions() that allows attackers to cause denial of service through crafted class files. Attackers can supply a class with a large method containing many long forward jumps, triggering unbounded toByteArray() recursion and a StackOverflowError during transformation.

CVE-2026-110260.description: OW2 ASM 3.0 before 9.11 contains a quadratic memory allocation vulnerability in MethodWriter.computeMaxStackAndLocal() and computeAllFrames() when using COMPUTE_MAXS or COMPUTE_FRAMES. Attackers can supply a crafted class file with thousands of overlapping exception handlers, causing excessive Edge allocations and an OutOfMemoryError that crashes the JVM.

CVE-2026-110261.description: OW2 ASM 3.0 before 9.11 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows attackers to exhaust CPU by supplying crafted class files processed with ClassWriter.COMPUTE_FRAMES. Attackers can craft methods that make the unbounded MethodWriter.computeAllFrames() fix point algorithm converge slowly, tying up transforming threads for unbounded time.

CVE-2026-110262.description: OW2 ASM 3.1 before 9.11 contains an excessive memory allocation vulnerability in the asm-commons AdviceAdapter that allows attackers to exhaust memory by supplying crafted class files. Attackers can craft bytecode with many forward jump targets in constructors, causing unbounded stack copies in forwardJumpStackFrames and allocation of hundreds of megabytes, leading to denial of service.

CVE-2026-110263.description: OW2 ASM 3.0 before 9.11 contains an uncontrolled recursion vulnerability in SignatureReader.parseType() that allows attackers to exhaust the stack via deeply nested generic type signatures. Attackers can supply a crafted class file with a long Signature attribute containing many nested type arguments to trigger a StackOverflowError during class transformation, causing denial of service.

CVE-2026-110270.description: OW2 ASM 3.0 before 9.11 contains an uncontrolled memory allocation vulnerability in the asm-commons JSRInlinerAdapter that inlines JSR/RET subroutines without memory or work limits. Attackers can supply a crafted class file with nested subroutines to force O(2^n) memory allocation, causing an OutOfMemoryError that crashes the JVM.

CVE-2026-110591.description: OW2 ASM 1.4.3 before 9.11 contains an excessive resource consumption vulnerability in Analyzer.analyze() that allows attackers to exhaust memory and CPU via crafted class files. Attackers can supply class files analysed through BasicVerifier, SimpleVerifier or SourceInterpreter to trigger unbounded per-instruction Frame allocation and fix point iterations, causing denial of service.

CVE-2026-110592.description: BottleCRM 0.30 through 1.14.5 contains an HTML injection vulnerability in render_invoice_template() that allows authenticated organization members to inject markup into custom-template invoice PDFs. Attackers can place HTML and CSS in notes, terms, client name or address fields to overlay totals, payee and payment instructions in PDFs served via download, public links and emails.

CVE-2026-110593.description: BottleCRM through 1.14.5 contains a server-side template injection vulnerability in the send_email Celery task, which compiles the user-supplied AccountEmail message_body with django.template.Template(). Authenticated organization members can submit template tags through POST /api/accounts/<id>/create_mail/ to disclose the rendering context and loaded Python modules, or block the shared Celery worker with nested loops.

CVE-2026-110594.description: BottleCRM 0.43 through 1.14.5 contains a regular expression denial of service vulnerability that allows authenticated organization administrators to block web workers via unbounded routing rule regex patterns. Attackers can create a routing rule with a catastrophically backtracking pattern evaluated by _match_condition() during case saves, exhausting workers shared across all tenants.

CVE-2026-110595.description: BottleCRM 0.45 through 1.14.5 contains an uncontrolled memory allocation vulnerability in _read_upload() that reads entire CSV uploads before enforcing the 5 MB limit. Authenticated users with mass-import permission can send oversized CSV files concurrently to /api/contacts/import/ and /api/cases/import/ endpoints to exhaust worker memory and trigger out-of-memory termination.

CVE-2026-110596.description: quirc through 1.2 contains an excessive-iteration vulnerability in find_alignment_pattern() in lib/identify.c that allows attackers to hang quirc_end() with a crafted image. Attackers can arrange three finder patterns producing a near-degenerate perspective transform, causing billions of region_code() iterations that exhaust CPU in applications decoding attacker-supplied QR images.

CVE-2026-110597.description: Tinyexr through 3.2.0 contains a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability in ParseEXRMultipartHeaderFromMemory() that allows attackers to read beyond buffers due to a stale remaining-size value. Attackers can supply a crafted multi-part EXR file whose later part headers bypass ReadAttribute() bounds checks, crashing applications or leaking adjacent heap memory into attribute values.

CVE-2026-110598.description: Libyal libpff through 20260926 contains an integer underflow in libpff_record_entry_get_multi_value() that allows attackers to trigger heap out-of-bounds reads via non-monotonic multi-value offsets. Attackers can craft PST, OST or PAB files with decreasing PT_MV_STRING8, PT_MV_UNICODE or PT_MV_BINARY offsets to crash libpff, pypff or pffexport and expose adjacent heap memory.

CVE-2026-110599.description: L-SMASH through 2.14.5 contains a double free vulnerability in hevc_setup_first_summary() and h264_setup_first_summary() in importer/nalu_imp.c that frees borrowed codec-specific objects on error paths. Attackers can supply a crafted Annex-B elementary stream lacking a parseable SPS to lsmash_read_file() or the boxdumper, remuxer, or muxer tools, causing use-after-free, heap corruption, and crashes.

CVE-2026-110600.description: xlsxio through 0.2.37 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in main_sheet_get_sheetfile_expat_callback_element_start() in lib/xlsxio_read.c that allows attackers to crash applications via crafted files. Attackers can supply a .xlsx file whose workbook.xml.rels contains a worksheet Relationship lacking an Id attribute, crashing the process when xlsxioread_sheet_open() is called.

CVE-2026-110601.description: libsixel before 1.8.7-r1 and 1.9.0 through 1.10.5 contains a heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in gif_init_frame() in src/fromgif.c, which never checks the GIF transparent color index against the palette size. Attackers can supply a crafted GIF with a small color table and large transparent index, processed with a background color set, to write bytes past the palette buffer, causing heap corruption or crashes.

CVE-2026-110602.description: libmspack through 0.11alpha contains an uninitialized pointer free vulnerability in kwajd_open() in mspack/kwajd.c that frees unzeroed filename and extra pointers on header read errors. Attackers can supply a truncated, empty, or wrong-signature KWAJ file to crash the process or obtain an arbitrary-free memory corruption primitive.

CVE-2026-110603.description: LASzip through 3.5.0 contains an invalid free vulnerability in laszip_read_header() that allows attackers to free uninitialized heap pointers via truncated variable length record data. Attackers can supply a crafted LAS/LAZ file with an inflated VLR count that, when opened and destroyed through the C API, crashes the process and corrupts the heap.

CVE-2026-110604.description: Mini-XML 4.0.0 through 4.0.6 contains an off-by-one stack out-of-bounds write in mxml_strtod() when the locale decimal point is not '.'. Attackers can supply XML with a 63-digit REAL value followed by '.' to write a NUL byte past the 64-byte stack buffer, corrupting stack memory or crashing the process.

CVE-2026-110605.description: libschrift through 0.10.2 contains a divide by zero vulnerability that allows attackers to crash applications by supplying a font with unitsPerEm of 0 in the head table. Attackers can provide a crafted TrueType font whose NaN glyph coordinates bypass clip_points(), causing an out-of-bounds raster read in draw_line() during sft_render() and crashing the process.

CVE-2026-110606.description: LibreCAD libdxfrw through LC2.2.0 (LibreCAD through 2.2.1.5) contains a stack-based out-of-bounds read vulnerability in dwgReader18::readFileHeader() caused by calling strlen on non-NUL-terminated buffers. Attackers can supply a crafted AC1018, AC1024 or AC1027 DWG file without NUL bytes in the decrypted header to read adjacent stack memory and crash the process.

CVE-2026-110607.description: BizSpring Shop through commit cf22d39daaf1 contains a payment verification bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated buyers to mark orders paid by calling the PaymentController.testPostPay handler. Attackers can generate a payment log via /member/payment/load and request /member/payment/test_post_pay_{paymentLogSn} to obtain goods without paying or settle other members' orders.

CVE-2026-110608.description: BizSpring Shop through commit cf22d39daaf1 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in the OrderController cancel and receive handlers that allows authenticated members to act on other members' orders by supplying their orderId. Attackers can cancel victims' pending orders to release allocated stock or confirm receipt of shipped orders, advancing fulfilment and settlement without the victim's consent.

CVE-2026-110609.description: Dromara Skyeye through commit 65d3ddcede70 contains an sql injection vulnerability that allows authenticated low-privileged users to inject SQL via the keyword parameter in the queryErpOrderItem MyBatis statement using raw ${} substitution. Attackers can send crafted keyword values to the queryWarehousingDetails or queryOutgoingDetails endpoints to extract database data, including other tenants' data, using boolean, UNION, error or time-based techniques.

CVE-2026-110610.description: ruoyi-vue-pro through 2026.09 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the yudao-module-ai image service that allows authenticated users to make the server fetch arbitrary URLs by supplying referImageUrl to the midjourney imagine endpoint. Attackers can force Hutool HttpUtil.downloadBytes() requests to loopback, private, or cloud metadata addresses to probe internal-only HTTP services and reach metadata endpoints.

CVE-2026-110611.description: REBUILD through 4.5.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in AiBot2Controller /aibot2 endpoints that act on a caller-supplied chatid without verifying ownership. Authenticated low-privilege users can supply another user's chatid to chat-init, chat-delete, chat-feedback, or chat-stream-stop to read, delete, exfiltrate, or interrupt AI assistant conversations.

CVE-2026-110612.description: vlife through 2.0.1 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to forge JWTs using the hardcoded HS256 signing key in TokenUtil. Attackers can sign a token with superUser=true and arbitrary groupIds claims to gain super administrator access to any URL on vlife instances.

CVE-2026-110613.description: youlai-mall through commit 9f62de8 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated members to view every customer's orders via the app order list endpoint. Attackers can page through the oms_order table using a self-registered account to read order ids, order_sn values, member ids, payment amounts, and order status.

CVE-2026-110614.description: Yiuman citrus through 0.15.0 contains an ORDER BY sql injection vulnerability in the citrus-support generic query framework that allows users to inject SQL via the sortBy request parameter. Attackers can reach any generic list route of controllers extending BaseQueryController or BaseQueryRestful to append unvalidated SQL to the ORDER BY clause and extract database contents using boolean- or time-based blind techniques.

CVE-2026-110615.description: jshERP through 3.6 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the POST /user/batchSetStatus endpoint that allows authenticated low-privilege users to change other users' account status. Attackers can submit crafted ids and status values to disable every non-owner account in their tenant, locking out administrators, or re-enable disabled accounts.

CVE-2026-110616.description: NullHub through 2026.5.29 contains a missing authentication vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to access the /api/* management API because the auth_token field defaults to null and is never assigned. Attackers sending requests without Authorization or Origin headers to non-loopback listeners can control agent instances, rewrite configurations including provider credentials, and manage cron jobs and MCP servers.

CVE-2026-110617.description: we-mp-rss through 1.5.3 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the /api/v1/wx/tools/export/download endpoint that allows unauthenticated attackers to download export archives because its authentication dependency is commented out. Attackers can supply an mp_id and guessable timestamp-based export filename to retrieve archives under data/docs, and set delete_after_download=true to delete them.

CVE-2026-110618.description: SmsForwarder through 3.5.0 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in its AndServer HTTP server that allows unauthenticated network attackers to invoke remote-control APIs. Attackers can call the default-enabled endpoints to read SMS, call logs and contacts, send SMS, and export or overwrite configuration via the clone API.

CVE-2026-110619.description: frp 0.41.0 through 0.71.1 contains a missing authentication vulnerability that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to access pprof debug endpoints because handlers are registered on the root mux outside Basic Authentication. Attackers can query /debug/pprof/ endpoints on frps dashboard or frpc admin listeners to obtain cmdline, goroutine stacks, heap profiles, and trigger CPU profiling.

CVE-2026-110620.description: Formbricks before 4.9.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in server actions like resetSurveyAction and updateSegmentAction that fail to verify resource ownership against the supplied organizationId. Authenticated owners or managers of any organization can pair their own organization identifier with victim resource IDs to delete survey responses, modify segments and quotas, or alter pending invitations.

CVE-2026-110621.description: Swetrix Cloud before 5.1.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in ProjectController.addProject that allows authenticated users to hijack arbitrary projects by moving them into their own organisation. Attackers can create an organisation and add a victim project by its public tracking ID to read analytics, change settings, or delete it.

CVE-2026-110622.description: Papermerge Core through 3.5.3 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated users to manipulate other users' pages because page management and OCR endpoints skip has_node_perm checks. Attackers knowing page UUIDs can call /pages/, /pages/move, or /pages/extract to rotate, delete, or extract victims' pages, and trigger OCR via /tasks/ocr.

CVE-2026-110623.description: Papermerge Core through 3.5.3 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the shared nodes API that allows authenticated users to share other users' documents by supplying arbitrary node UUIDs. Attackers can call POST /shared-nodes or PATCH /shared-nodes/access/{node_id} to grant themselves any role, then read, modify, or delete victims' documents and revoke existing shares.

CVE-2026-110624.description: Papermerge Core through 3.5.3 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated users to list other groups' tags and document types by supplying a group_id parameter. Attackers who know a group's UUID can query GET /tags/all or GET /document-types/all, which skip the user_belongs_to check, to disclose metadata of groups they do not belong to.

CVE-2026-110625.description: ClipBucket v5 through 5.5.3-#206 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in admin_area/flagged_item.php via the unencoded type GET parameter. Attackers can send crafted flagged_item.php?type= links to logged-in administrators or moderators to execute injected script in the admin panel origin.

CVE-2026-110626.description: ClipBucket v5 through 5.5.3-#206 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in admin_area/language_settings.php via the unencoded edit_language GET parameter. Attackers can send administrators with basic_settings permission a crafted link whose payload is echoed into a hidden input, executing script in the admin panel origin.

CVE-2026-110627.description: ClipBucket v5 through 5.5.3-#206 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in admin_area/index.php that allows attackers to inject HTML via the val parameter in mode=add_todo. Attackers can lure a logged-in administrator into submitting a cross-site POST form without CSRF protection, executing script in the admin panel origin.

CVE-2026-110628.description: Kan 0.5.5 through 0.6.0 contains an unauthenticated server-side request forgery vulnerability in the /api/download/attatchment route due to an incomplete fix for CVE-2026-32255. When S3_ENDPOINT is unset, attackers can pass arbitrary url query parameters to fetch() to read internal services, localhost ports, and cloud instance metadata.

CVE-2026-110629.description: VentureDrake Laravel CRM before 2.4.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated users to bypass Spatie role permissions through Livewire action methods. Read-only users can invoke delete, won, lost or reopen methods on components like DealIndex, or use unguarded Activities and Products routes, to modify deals, quotes, orders and invoices.

CVE-2026-110630.description: VentureDrake Laravel CRM before 2.4.0 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in user management that allows authenticated administrators to assign unrestricted roles via Role::find. Attackers with user-management access can assign the Owner role or other teams' roles and delete cross-team users through the unscoped UserIndex delete() method.

CVE-2026-110631.description: Komodo through 2.3.3 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in the Periphery agent that allows unauthenticated attackers to connect as a trusted Core because empty core_public_keys and passkeys lists fail open by default. Attackers reaching port 8120 can present any generated keypair to issue Periphery API requests, including terminal sessions and container operations, executing commands on managed hosts typically as root.

CVE-2026-110632.description: Report One MyReport Updater through 2.1.1 exposes an unauthenticated gRPC service on TCP port 9095 that allows remote attackers to redirect the SYSTEM updater by invoking the UpdateConfigReferent method. Attackers can point the updater to a malicious reference server serving modified module archives with matching MD5 digests to write files and execute code as SYSTEM.

CVE-2026-110633.description: MyReport Updater through 2.1.1 contains a local privilege escalation vulnerability that allows low-privileged users to make the SYSTEM updater service install attacker-supplied archives into arbitrary directories. Attackers can use UpdaterManager.exe over gRPC to set a malicious reference server and installLocation, planting a DLL like HID.dll loaded by osk.exe to gain SYSTEM privileges.

CVE-2026-110634.description: git-diff before 2.0.7 contains an OS command injection vulnerability that allows attackers to execute shell commands by supplying crafted strings to the gitDiff API. Attackers who control a diffed document string can embed $(cmd) or backtick substitutions that shelljs.exec evaluates, running commands with Node.js process privileges.

CVE-2026-110635.description: webp-converter before 3.0.0 contains an OS command injection vulnerability in src/webpconverter.js helpers that run libwebp binaries via execFile with shell enabled. Attackers controlling file names or option strings passed to cwebp, dwebp, gwebp, or webpmux functions can inject shell metacharacters to execute OS commands as the Node.js process.

CVE-2026-110636.description: pypdftk through 0.5 contains an OS command injection vulnerability in fill_form(), dump_data_fields(), and pdftk_cmd_util() that builds shell commands from caller-supplied paths. Attackers controlling pdf_path or out_file can inject shell metacharacters interpreted by subprocess.Popen with shell=True to execute OS commands as the Python process.

CVE-2026-110637.description: buildebooks before 0.2.2 contains an OS command injection vulnerability in lib/kindle.js that allows attackers to execute commands by supplying a crafted EPUB file name passed to kindlegen via child_process.exec. Attackers can craft a book project with a malicious front-matter filename or project folder name and kindle: true to execute OS commands as the user running buildebooks.

CVE-2026-110638.description: doc-recog through 1.1.6 contains an OS command injection vulnerability that allows attackers to execute commands by supplying crafted document paths to recog() or tag(). Attackers can embed $(...) or backtick command substitution in the file path, which DocData._readPDF passes to a shell-based pdftotext exec call, running commands with Node.js process privileges.

CVE-2026-110639.description: @mborne/extract before 0.2.1 contains an OS command injection vulnerability that allows attackers to execute commands by supplying shell metacharacters in archivePath or targetDir options. Attackers controlling these values passed to extract() can inject commands into unquoted shelljs exec() strings in the unzip, 7z, tar-bz2 and gz extractors, running them with Node.js process privileges.

CVE-2026-110640.description: Whisper-node through 1.1.1 contains an OS command injection vulnerability that allows attackers to execute commands by supplying crafted filePath or whisperOptions.language values to whisper(). Attackers can inject shell metacharacters or $() substitution into the command string built by createCppCommand() and run via shelljs exec() to execute commands with Node.js process privileges.

CVE-2026-110641.description: @runnerty/executor-decompress through 3.1.1 contains an OS command injection vulnerability that allows attackers to execute commands by supplying crafted archive file names to compress_file. Attackers who can name a file dropped into a watched directory can inject $() substitutions or unquoted shell metacharacters into shelljs exec() calls, running commands with Runnerty process privileges.

CVE-2026-110642.description: xhtml2pdf before 0.2.19 contains an OS command injection vulnerability in pisa.startViewer() that allows attackers to execute commands by interpolating unescaped file names into os.system. Attackers can supply an input file whose name contains a double quote and shell metacharacters, which runs OS commands as the invoking user when the pisa tool is used with -s/--start-viewer.

CVE-2026-110643.description: transcribe2texts through 1.0.6 contains an OS command injection vulnerability that allows attackers to execute commands by supplying crafted audioPath values to transcribeAudio(). Attackers can inject $() or backtick substitution or a closing quote into the unescaped path passed to child_process.exec() to run commands with Node.js process privileges.

CVE-2026-110644.description: nodejs-whisper through 0.3.1 contains an OS command injection vulnerability in convertToWavType() that allows attackers to execute commands by supplying crafted audio file paths. Attackers can provide file names containing $() command substitution or closing quotes, which are interpolated into an ffmpeg command run via shelljs exec(), executing OS commands with Node.js process privileges.

CVE-2026-110645.description: Video-stitch before 2.0.0-beta.1 contains an OS command injection vulnerability that allows attackers to execute commands by supplying file names interpolated unquoted into shell-executed ffmpeg command lines. Attackers who influence file names passed to concat(), cut(), or merge() can inject shell metacharacters to run commands with the Node.js process privileges.

CVE-2026-110646.description: Beganovich snappdf from 1.1.0 before 6.1.0 contains an OS command injection vulnerability on Windows that allows attackers to run commands by influencing the rendered URL. Attackers can supply cmd.exe metacharacters such as & in the setUrl() value, which executeOnWindows() passes unescaped to PHP exec(), executing commands as the PHP process.

CVE-2026-110647.description: Turnpress through 0.4.2 contains an OS command injection vulnerability that allows attackers to execute shell commands by supplying .docx files with crafted names. The convertDocxToHtml function in src/converter.ts invokes pandoc through execa with shell:true, so shell metacharacters in the --docx path run with the victim's privileges during convert or create.

CVE-2026-110648.description: @offactory/compress-fonts before 1.1.1 contains an OS command injection vulnerability that allows attackers to execute shell commands by supplying font files with crafted names. Font paths are interpolated unquoted into a FontForge command run through child_process.execSync, so shell metacharacters in file names execute commands with the Node.js process privileges.

CVE-2026-110649.description: Stills before 25.24.2 contains an OS command injection vulnerability that allows attackers to execute shell commands by supplying crafted media file paths. Attackers can name a media file with $(...) or backticks to execute operating system commands with Node.js process privileges when ffmpeg, ffprobe, gifsicle, or convert runs.

CVE-2026-110650.description: The thumbnail Python package through 1.5 contains an OS command injection vulnerability in generate_thumbnail() that allows attackers to execute commands by supplying shell metacharacters in file paths. Attackers who control a file name passed to generate_thumbnail, such as an uploaded file, can inject commands into os.system() calls running ffmpeg, convert or unoconv with the Python process privileges.

CVE-2026-15176.description:
A vulnerability exists in NGINX Plus and NGINX Open Source when a location is configured that uses the alias directive together with rewrite and a set or return directive referencing the $request_filename variable. Alternatively, the same result could be achieved when the $request_filename variable is used in an access log format directive. An unauthenticated attacker along with conditions beyond their control can exploit this vulnerability by sending crafted HTTP requests. This may cause a heap buffer overflow in the NGINX worker process leading to a restart. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR.

Impact:
This vulnerability may allow remote attackers to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the NGINX system or to possibly trigger a code execution. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.




Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

CVE-2026-25946.description: When OpenID sign-in is enabled, Gitea accepts a user-supplied OpenID URL and performs discovery requests without validating the destination against internal network addresses. An unauthenticated remote attacker can cause the server to contact loopback or private-network HTTP services. This can expose internal service behavior and enable interaction with resources that are not directly reachable by the attacker.

CVE-2026-53612.description: util-linux is a random collection of Linux utilities. In util-linux 2.39 through 2.41.4 and 2.42 through 2.42.1, the SUID `mount` utility's `hook_owner.c` post-mount hook performs path-based `chmod()` and `lchown()` operations on a previously validated mount target. A local low-privileged user authorized by an `/etc/fstab` entry with `user` or `users` and an `X-mount.mode`, `X-mount.owner`, or `X-mount.group` option can use `renameat2(RENAME_EXCHANGE)` to race a writable ancestor of the target and redirect the privileged ownership or mode change to a root-owned path, potentially gaining root privileges. This issue is fixed in 2.41.5 and 2.42.2.

CVE-2026-53613.description: util-linux is a random collection of Linux utilities. In util-linux 2.17 through 2.41.6 and 2.42 through 2.42.3, and in 2.42.4 when the legacy `mount(2)` path is used without `/proc`, restricted non-root `mount` requests validate an `/etc/fstab` target before the mount operation re-resolves that pathname. A local low-privileged user authorized by an fstab `user` or `users` entry whose target has an attacker-writable ancestor can use `renameat2(RENAME_EXCHANGE)` to swap a path component and redirect an authorized mount to a root-owned location, such as mounting attacker-controlled content over `/etc/sudoers.d`, and thereby gain root privileges. Versions 2.41.5 and 2.42.2 pin targets for the new mount API, and 2.42.4 pins legacy targets through `/proc/self/fd`; the documented legacy fallback without `/proc` remains affected.

CVE-2026-59766.description: Gitea's starred-repository and tracked-time API endpoints do not re-check current repository permissions before returning data associated with the requesting user. A user whose access to a private repository has been revoked can still retrieve repository metadata through /api/v1/user/starred and private issue titles through /api/v1/user/times. The disclosure depends on relationships or tracked-time entries created before access was revoked.

CVE-2026-59774.description: Gitea's Org-mode markup renderer processes INCLUDE directives supplied to the repository markup endpoint without preventing access to server-side files. An unauthenticated attacker can use a suitable public repository to read files accessible to the Gitea service account. If the disclosed files include app.ini and its INTERNAL_TOKEN, the attacker can chain the disclosure with internal logger access to modify a Git hook and execute commands as the Gitea service account.

CVE-2026-60008.description: Gitea's Jupyter notebook renderer inserts the notebook's language_info.name metadata into a CSS class attribute while disabling sanitization and rendering directly in the main document without an iframe sandbox. A malicious repository notebook can supply multiple CSS classes that create a viewport-covering overlay and intercept clicks when another user views it.
